relations.note: Llano argued writers imported and reshaped Basajaun as the Busgosu.
Jove described the Busgosu as the Asturian equivalent of the pagan Faun.
relations.source: Jove, Mitos y supersticiones de Asturias

relations.note: Later summaries compare him with Pan through goat anatomy and woodland sexuality.
His goatlike body and pursuit of women prompted comparison with satyrs.
relations.source: Jove, Mitos y supersticiones de Asturias

relations.note: Later mythographers compare Busgosu with Silvanus through their woodland functions.
Menéndez Pidal equated Slavic woodland beings with the Busgosos of Asturias.
Menéndez Pidal equated Polkans with the Busgosos of Asturias.
Menéndez Pidal included Berstuk among Slavic beings equated with Asturian Busgosos.
Popular accounts speculate that Busgosu descends from the horned Celtic god.
Modern speculation proposes Vosegus as a name or functional ancestor.
Popular synthesis alleges that the Asturian horned god evolved into Busgosu.
Later regional syntheses increasingly conflate the Cantabrian woodland helper with Busgosu.
Cabal linked masked Guirrio traditions with the Busgosu and Faun pattern.
